summary.headline: Stanley Lifestyles Q2 FY27 revenue rose 1.6% YoY to Rs. 10,706 lakhs and EBITDA margin was 18.6%, with retail same-store sales still negative.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs. 10,706 lakhs, up from Rs. 10,542 lakhs a year earlier and 7.8% sequentially from Rs. 9,935 lakhs in Q1. H1 revenue fell to Rs. 20,641 lakhs from Rs. 21,409 lakhs. EBITDA was Rs. 1,989 lakhs (18.6% margin), up 15.5% QoQ, with rupee depreciation pressuring gross margin. Management attributed retail softness to delayed residential handovers and said same-store sales growth at older COCO stores is negative. Management is betting on QCO-driven B2B demand, the new Superlative large-format store and a return to double-digit growth after stabilisation.

financial_highlights.value: About Rs. 170 crores (as cited by analyst; management said cash position remains strong)
Typically 7% to 9% of revenue, occasionally up to 10%

segments.name: Retail COCO stores
segments.commentary: Store count is about 70, with 3 opened and 3 closed in Q2. Management said same-store sales growth is negative and 15% to 18% of stores are loss-making, mostly under 18 months old.

segments.name: B2B manufacturing
segments.commentary: Management said recent sales growth came mainly from B2B. Existing facilities could support about 2x current revenue, and the company is preparing for higher B2B volumes tied to QCO.

segments.name: Superlative Living (large format)
segments.commentary: First 72,000 sq ft store opened in Hyderabad about 60 days before the call, with Rs. 7 to 8 crores of pipeline built. Management guided Rs. 70 to 80 crores revenue in years 2 to 3.

segments.name: International and new markets
segments.commentary: First overseas store is Stanley Boutique in Colombo, Sri Lanka, run with Singer Sri Lanka PLC. A Sofas & More store opened in Jaipur, entering Rajasthan.

guidance_outlook: Management expects order book and delivery pipeline to strengthen from Q3 or early Q4 FY27 as residential handovers progress.
Management says revenue should return to double-digit growth after a quarter or two of stabilisation, with expansion to follow.

Management targets about 20% EBITDA margin after rentals for mature stores (pre-Ind AS basis). Superlative stores are expected to break even in 2 to 3 quarters, with breakeven from the fourth quarter.
Management declined to give H2 profitability colour and said it would update at the next earnings call.
Management says Rs. 2.83 crore exceptional charge may be reversed in Q3 after recovery efforts against an ex-company secretary.
capex_capacity: Existing manufacturing capacity can support about 2x current revenue, subject to product mix and warehousing of raw material.
Superlative Living: 72,000 sq ft Hyderabad store opened; plan to convert smaller Stanley stores in Delhi, Mumbai, Hyderabad and Bangalore into large-format hubs, with Sofas & More as spokes.
Recurring store opex is about 12% to 13% of sales currently, targeted at 10% to 11% when mature, and 15% to 16% expected for new Superlative stores.
Proposed amalgamation of subsidiaries and step-down subsidiaries into the listed company is in progress.
Sofas & More rebranded format without the Stanley name is being prepared in Hyderabad, expected to go live in about 45 days.
demand_pricing: Customer base is mainly new-home buyers in premium and luxury residential projects, and delayed possessions are extending purchase cycles.

Imported furniture faced QCO disruption from August 2026; the government extended the deadline to 1 January 2027, and about 40 more products were put out for comment with finalisation expected around 17 December.
Management estimates the imported leather sofa and recliner market at about US$100 million, served by about 800 retailers, roughly 80% of which depend on imports.
Festival-season discounting followed importers' front-loaded inventory, creating short-term price pressure across the industry.
About 75% to 80% of orders are custom-made, and management says revenue per sq ft is not a meaningful comparison metric.

qa_highlights.question: Is the delayed handover demand in the order book, and how much can current capacity support?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book is about Rs. 60 crores versus about Rs. 53 crores a year ago; existing capacity can support almost 2x current revenue, which an analyst put at about Rs. 800 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise faster than revenue, and what will lift H2 EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudhir Iyer cited increments, capitalised NPD staff costs now being amortised, and senior management hiring; management said it was too early to give H2 colour.

qa_highlights.question: Same-store sales growth for older stores and why COCO is not growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said same-store sales growth is negative and offered to share older-store data by email; COCO stores are being converted to a complete home solutions format.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for share buyback given about Rs. 170 crores cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Sudhir Iyer said buyback is not being explored currently but would be considered.

qa_highlights.question: What is the recovery status of the Rs. 2.83 crore exceptional item?
qa_highlights.answer: An ex-company secretary involved in the fraud has been arrested and has confessed; recovery is under way and the charge may reverse in Q3, with no net financial loss expected to the company.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA and opex levels should be expected from large-format stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is about 20% EBITDA after rentals on a pre-Ind AS basis; recurring costs of 12% to 13% of sales are expected to fall to 10% to 11% at maturity, with breakeven in 2 to 3 quarters.

risks_watch: Residential possession delays may keep retail conversion cycles extended beyond Q3 or Q4 FY27.
Same-store sales are negative at older COCO stores, and 15% to 18% of stores are loss-making.
Rupee depreciation is compressing gross margin, and employee costs are rising faster than revenue.
QCO timing (1 January 2027 deadline and the final product list) determines the size and timing of B2B opportunity.
Revenue CAGR has been flat since listing, against an earlier target of Rs. 1,000 crores in 1,000 working days, which management now says is still the plan.
Pending confirmation of the Rs. 2.83 crore fraud-related recovery in Q3.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term structural opportunity (QCO, Superlative, B2B) but cautious on near-term retail; management repeatedly deferred numeric answers (H2 outlook, same-store sales, buyback) and offered email follow-ups.
key_quotes: Our existing manufacturing capacities are good enough to do almost 2x our revenues, provided we might need to shift some of the raw material out of our facility into a warehouse or something like that.
We have decided that we will shut down smaller Stanley stores and come up with one mega store which will cater to complete home solution.

Good news to the shareholders is we were able to arrest the ex-company secretary who was involved in this financial fraud, and he has confessed to the police, and we are in the process of recovering that.
Good question. Let me answer for this. It is a good thought, and to be honest with you, currently we do not explore that.

Festival-season discounting followed importers' front-loaded inventory ahead of QCO; short-term price pressure industry-wide, not a clear one-off to revenue

quality.why: Q2 revenue grew only 1.6% YoY (Rs. 10,706 lakhs vs Rs. 10,542 lakhs) with the brief giving no volume or price split and H1 down about 3.6%; management attributes recent growth mainly to B2B, but retail same-store sales are negative and 15-18% of stores are loss-making, so the underlying growth is weak rather than one-off-driven.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 18.6% (up 15.5% QoQ) but rupee depreciation compresses gross margin and employee costs (Rs. 14.29 cr) are rising faster than revenue; mature-store target is about 20% after rentals, and management declined H2 colour.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Superlative 72,000 sq ft Hyderabad store already opened (~60 days before call), with plans to convert Stanley stores in Delhi, Mumbai, Hyderabad and Bangalore into large-format hubs; Sofas & More Hyderabad rebrand expected in about 45 days.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book about Rs. 60 cr vs about Rs. 53 cr a year ago (+13%) and H1 revenue down about 3.6%, with same-store sales negative and 3 stores closed in Q2; growth depends on handovers and QCO timing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Existing manufacturing can support about 2x current revenue, so no new plant is needed for now; capex was not discussed beyond store conversions.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give H2 profitability colour and gave no FY27 revenue number, only that double-digit growth should return after a quarter or two of stabilisation.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue down about 3.6%, same-store sales negative, 15% to 18% of stores loss-making, and handover delays may extend beyond Q3 or Q4 FY27.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Sofas & More rebranded format in Hyderabad expected to go live in about 45 days, and the Superlative large-format conversions are planned; Rajasthan entry via Jaipur store already opened.

rows.label: QCO-driven B2B demand on imported furniture
rows.why: QCO deadline extended to 1 January 2027 with about 40 more products under comment and finalisation around 17 December; about 80% of ~800 retailers depend on imports in a roughly US$100 million market, but timing is uncertain.

rows.label: Superlative stores reach breakeven
rows.why: Management expects breakeven from the fourth quarter (2 to 3 quarters) with store opex of 15% to 16% of sales for new Superlative stores versus 12% to 13% for existing stores.

rows.label: Rs. 2.83 crore exceptional charge reversal
rows.why: Recovery under way after an ex-company secretary was arrested and confessed; management says the charge may reverse in Q3, but that depends on recovery confirmation.

tone.note: Management was confident on QCO, Superlative and B2B structural opportunity but cautious on near-term retail, deferring H2 outlook, same-store sales and buyback questions with email follow-ups; analysts pressed on employee cost growth, negative same-store sales and cash deployment.
